'''Sven Bertil Erlander''' (25 May 1934 – 13 June 2021)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ersa.org/2021/06/15/in-memoriam-professor-sven-erlander/|title = In memoriam: Professor Sven Erlander – ERSA| date=15 June 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://liu.se/nyhet/sven-erlander-har-avlidit|title = Sven Erlander har avlidit}}</ref> was a Swedish mathematician and academic.

==Biography==
Erlander was the son of [[Tage Erlander]], who was the Prime Minister of Sweden from 1946 to 1969. He published several of his father's diaries.<ref>[http://www.nt.se/arkiv/2001/08/18/Kultur/1330178/Statsminister-i--tre-rum-och-k%F6k-.aspx Article in Norrköpings Tidningar] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120907084443/http://www.nt.se/arkiv/2001/08/18/Kultur/1330178/Statsminister-i--tre-rum-och-k%F6k-.aspx |date=7 September 2012 }} (in Swedish)</ref>

He received his PhD in mathematics from [[Stockholm University]] in 1968. In 1971 he became a professor in [[Optimization (mathematics)|Optimisation]] at [[Linköping University]]. In Linköping he was [[department head]] of the Mathematics department from 1973 to 1976, and [[Dean (education)|dean]] of the [[Linköping Institute of Technology|Institute of Technology]] between 1978 and 1983.

In 1983–1995 he was the [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of Linköping University.<ref name="CV">[http://www.mai.liu.se/~sverl/cv.html CV at Linköping University] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724010133/http://www.mai.liu.se/~sverl/cv.html |date=24 July 2011 }}</ref>

== Awards ==
* Member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]], 1983
* Honorary Doctorate, [[Gdańsk University]], Poland

== Publications ==
* ''Cost-Minimizing Choice Behavior in Transportation Planning'', monograph, [[Springer Verlag]], 2010.
